gloss: to take up (a position); to assume

definitions.gloss: to take up (a position); to assume (a role)
definitions.explanation: To start occupying a position, job, or role. Often used for taking on new responsibilities or positions.
To settle into bed or go to sleep. Common in formal or literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{職|しょく}に{就|つ}いた。
examples.english: I took up a new job.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}の{座|ざ}に{就|つ}く。
examples.english: To assume the position of president.

examples.japanese: {床|とこ}に{就|つ}く{時間|じかん}だ。
examples.english: It's time to go to bed.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし}).

PATTERNS:
・〜に{就|つ}く (to take up ~, to assume ~)
・{職|しょく}に{就|つ}く (to get a job)
・{席|せき}に{就|つ}く (to take one's seat)
・{床|とこ}に{就|つ}く (to go to bed - formal)

RELATED WORDS:
・{就職|しゅうしょく}する (to get employed)
・{就任|しゅうにん}する (to take office)
